## Problem
Discovered during plan-review of the sibling "rank aggregation by priority" ticket
(beaming-snively-urial): `src/rebar/llm/spec_scan.py:13,137` imports `_severity_rank` from
`aggregate.py` directly and sorts its own findings list by it
(`findings.sort(key=_severity_rank, reverse=True)`). `spec_scan.py`'s findings come straight
from the "spec-alignment" LLM reviewer's structured output via `finalize_findings`
(`findings.py`) -- they never pass through `pass3_decide` and never get `priority`, unlike
the review-kernel/DET-tier findings the rest of this epic migrates.

## OBSOLETED
Follow-up research (see epic pink-complex-xenurine session log) established that
`findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES`/`normalize_finding`/`Finding.severity` vocabulary is used
by an entire completion-verification module cluster (`completion_reconcile.py`,
`completion_child_gate.py`, `epic_bug_screen.py`, `workflow/gate_ops.py`,
`workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py`) that hardcodes `severity` as its ONLY signal, with
no priority/decision/impact alternative available. Deleting `findings.py`'s shared severity
vocabulary (the sibling cleanup ticket byzantine-spinelike-penguin's original plan) would have
broken that entire cluster. The corrected epic architecture keeps `findings.py`'s shared
severity vocabulary intact -- only the review-kernel (`pass3_decide`) stops STAMPING severity
onto its own emitted findings. `spec_scan.py`'s `_severity_rank`-based ranking reads this
still-present shared vocabulary and is therefore never broken by this epic. This ticket's
premise no longer holds; no migration is needed.

## Approach (superseded, retained for context)
Would have mapped spec_scan's severity string to a numeric priority via a fixed ordinal
mapping (any unrecognized/missing severity defaulting to 0.0, info-equivalent) before sorting
by priority instead of `_severity_rank`. Not implemented -- obsoleted per above.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Confirmed via the epic's corrected architecture that `findings.py`'s severity
  vocabulary remains intact and `spec_scan.py` requires no change.

## Testing
Not applicable -- no code change made.
